title: Multi-GPU concurrency and regression test suite for distributed inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible end-to-end benchmarking and CI-driven regression detection suite that validates multi-GPU distributed inference configurations (tensor and pipeline parallelism). The goal is to reliably measure steady-state tokens/sec and tail latency (p95/p99) across representative workloads, detect regressions automatically on PRs and mainline changes, and provide a live dashboard with historical trends and per-model baselines.
acceptance_criteria: Automated suite runs in CI and completes for target configs (1/2/4/8 GPU) within time budget
Collected metrics include tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit rate, memory utilization, and GPU SM utilization
Regression detector alerts on >5% drop in tokens/sec or >10% increase in p95 relative to baseline for a given model/config
Results stored in perf DB and surfaced in dashboard with 90-day history and anchors for releases
Integration tests that run lightweight smoke for every PR and nightly full-suite runs
Playbooks documented for triage and rollback if a performance regression is detected
test_plan: Workloads: mix of small (max 256 tokens), medium (1024 tokens), and long-range (4096 tokens) prompts; include streaming and non-streaming paths
Model variants: float16 fp16 baseline, Q4/8 quantized variants, 1x tensor-parallel, 2x/4x pipeline-parallel mixes
Concurrency sweep: 1..256 concurrent requests with steady arrival processes to exercise batching and KV cache behavior
Metrics collection: per-request latency histogram, tokens/sec aggregated by model+config, GPU metrics via DCGM, exporter to Prometheus + PerfDB
Synthetic vs replay: nightlies use replay traces sampled from production (anonymized); CI uses deterministic synthetic traces to keep runs fast
Regression detection: use historical baseline per-model+config with rolling window; signal-to-noise reduction with bootstrap resampling
Acceptance thresholds: regression if median tokens/sec drop >=5% with p<0.05 or p95 increases >=10%
Failure modes: noisy runs flagged and retried up to 2 times; persistent failures create triage task with logs and perf artifacts
architecture_notes: Harness runs on Dedicated ephemeral pools to isolate noise from multi-tenant interference
Coordinator service will orchestrate config matrix and collect KV cache warmup states before measurement
Use per-step warmup period (e.g., 120s) to reach steady-state before sampling tokens/sec
Leverage existing tensor/pipeline scheduling hooks in runtime to pin kernels and collect per-stage timings
Results emitted in JSONL and ingested into PerfDB with provenance (git sha, branch, config)
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Triage meeting — agreed scope and success metrics. Decided to prioritize stability of p95 detection over absolute tokens/sec comparisons due to environment noise.
2026-02-26: Prototype coordinator implemented that can launch 1/2/4 GPU runs and collect DCGM metrics. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2107
2026-03-03: Baseline collection for model 'rw-7b-v1' completed on 4x A100 dedicated pool; stored sample in PerfDB: perfdb://runs/20344/baseline
2026-03-07: Design review with SRE and Runtime — agreed on warmup heuristics (2 min) and bootstrap-based regression test. Notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Multi-GPU+Perf+Suite
2026-03-10: CI integration spike completed: smoke job added to GitHub Actions that runs abbreviated suite for PRs. Smoke job PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-config/pull/389

2026-03-12: Nightly full-suite scheduling configured; first nightly run generated noisy 8-GPU p95 outliers suspected due to noisy host. Follow-up: isolate to dedicated hosts and re-run. Artifact: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/perf/multi-gpu-suite?orgId=1
risks_and_mitigation: High variance on shared hardware — mitigation: run on Dedicated ephemeral pools and increase sample size
Long run times for full matrix — mitigation: stratified nightlies and fast smoke in PRs
False positives from regression detector due to workload changes — mitigation: require repeatable signal across 3 consecutive runs before auto-blocking releases
Data volume and storage costs — mitigation: store aggregated summaries in PerfDB and keep raw traces for 30 days
next_steps: Stabilize nightly harness by pinning host images and re-running 8-GPU jobs (assigned to Miguel)
Add model-agnostic baselining job that can synthesize warmup sequences for new model onboarding
Implement auto-triage playbook: attach top 5 correlated metrics (GPU mem, SM%, KV hit) when a regression is detected
Finalize dashboard widgets and alert rules and hand off to Observability for maintenance
